'''Boman Framji Chhapgar''' (1 January 1931 – 5 August 2018<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prayar Hall Trust|date=5 August 2018 |url=http://prayerhalltrust.org/2018/08/05/dr-boman-framji-chhapgar/}}</ref>) was an Indian [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] who specialized in [[carcinology]]. The author of popular accounts on marine biology under the pen-name of "beefsea", several new species of crab, [[mantis shrimp]] and [[fish]]es have been described by him.

==Early life and education==
Boman Framji Chhapgar was born on 1 January 1931 in [[Bombay]] to [[Parsi]] parents Banoobai and Framji Chhapgar.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marine biologist {{!}} Reader's Forum|url=https://www.parsiana.com/current-issue/articles.aspx?id=axfEWZvMYgM=&issue=368|access-date=2020-10-11|website=parsiana.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Trust|first=Prayer Hall|date=2018-08-05|title=DR. BOMAN FRAMJI CHHAPGAR|url=http://prayerhalltrust.org/2018/08/05/dr-boman-framji-chhapgar/|access-date=2020-10-11|website=Prayer Hall Trust|language=en-US}}</ref> After completing school at Bharda New High School in 1944, he studied microbiology and zoology at [[St. Xavier's College, Mumbai|St. Xavier's College]], graduating in 1948 with microbiology as his main subject.<ref>{{Cite web|title=" A Hundred More Years To Go": A Tribute To Dr. Chhapgar. Sanctuary Asia article by Vardhan Patankar|url=https://www.sanctuaryasia.com/magazines/features/10196--a-hundred-more-years-to-go-a-tribute-to-dr-chhapgar.html}}</ref> He also obtained a second [[Bachelor of Science]] (Honours) degree from the [[The Institute of Science, Mumbai|Royal Institute of Science]], Bombay with [[zoology]]. In 1951 he joined the Taraporewala Marine Biological Station (attached to the [[Taraporewala Aquarium]]), affiliated to the [[University of Bombay]] as its first MSc student. In 1954 he was awarded the Shri Vicaji D. B. Taraporevala Senior Research scholarship. He registered for a PhD in 1972 completing it in 1976. In 1957, he was selected for the [[UNESCO]] Marine Biology Refresher Course, which he successfully completed the following year.<ref name=obit>{{cite journal|author=Krishnan, Smita| title=Boman Framji Chhapgar. January 1, 1931 – August 5, 2018| journal=Hornbill|page=40|year=2018|issue=October–December}}</ref>

He also trained as a [[scuba diver]] and took an interest in [[scouting]] and hiking.

==Career==
Dr Chhapgar joined the Department of Fisheries, Bombay State in 1955 as a junior research assistant. He moved on to become a senior research assistant, biologist, superintendent of fisheries and later an assistant director of fisheries, taking up postings at a various locations, including [[Kolhapur]], [[Satara district|Satara]] and [[Sangli]] Districts. From 1959 to 1965 he served as [[curator]] of the [[Taraporewala Aquarium]].

He participated in the International Indian Ocean Expedition (1959–64)<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.scor-int.org/Historical%20Documents/Snider-Discovery.pdf|author=Snider, RG|title=The International Indian Ocean Expedition 1959-64|year=1961|journal=Discovery|pages=114–117}}</ref> aboard the [[USS Williamsburg (AGC-369)|USS Anton Bruun]] (from Madras to Vishakhapatnam) and [[HMS Andromeda (F57)|INS Kistna]] (Cochin to Port Blair to Madras, 1961–1965) and on the maiden cruise of the Indian oceanographic vessel [[ORV Sagar Kanya]] (from Marmagao to Mombasa) in 1983 to study the monsoon in the [[Arabian Sea]].<ref name=obit /><ref name=":0">Kamolika Roy Chowhury (2018). A star is gone. [https://spectrumsciencemagazine.blogspot.com/2018/11/spectrum-science-newsletter-september.html Spectrum science magazine], Issue 7, september 2018</ref>

In 1973 he joined the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] to study aquatic [[radioactivity]] and its impact on the marine environment. He retired in 1987.{{Citation needed|date=September 2010}}

==Species described==
Even as a research student, he described two new species of crabs and a new form of another. The crab species were described in the Records of the Indian Museum in 1956 (''Pinnotheres vicajii'', ''Pseudograpsus intermedius'', ''Leptodius euglyptus quadrispinosus''.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Chhapgar,. B. F.|year=1955| title= On two new species and a new variety of crabs (Decapoda: Brachyura) from Bombay State|journal= Rec. Indian Mus.|volume=53 |issue=1&2|pages= 251–260}}</ref> The first two species of crabs were discovered in the sea off Bombay while the third was found in the [[Okha, India|Okha]] region of [[Gujarat]].

In 1966, he described two [[mantis shrimp]]s from Bombay in the genus ''Squilla'' (now ''[[Clorida]]'').<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Chhapgar, BF & SR Sane|year=1966|title= Two new species of Squilla (Stomatopod) from Bombay|journal= Crustaceana|volume=12 |issue=1|pages= 1–8|doi=10.1163/156854067X00657}}</ref>

After his retirement he described, along with S. R. Sane, a new species of fish ''[[Puntius setnai]]'' from Goa.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Chhapgar, B.F. & S.R. Sane |year=1992|title= A new fish of the genus ''Puntius'' Hamilton (Ostariophysi: Cyprinidae) from Goa|journal=J. Bombay Nat. Hist. Soc.|volume=89|issue=3|pages=357–359}}</ref>

==Achievements and honours==
Chhapgar specialized in the Decapoda particularly the marine species in the infraorder Brachyura.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Directory of Zoological Taxonomists of the World|author=Blackwelder RE & RM Blackwelder|year=1961|publisher=Southern Illinois University Press, Illinois|url=https://archive.org/stream/directoryofzoolo00blac#page/150/mode/1up/}}</ref> He was elected a Life Fellow of the International Oceanographic Foundation, for his "contributions to the advancement and extension of knowledge and discovery in oceanography and the marine sciences". A portrait of him is included in the Gallery of Carcinologists in the [[Smithsonian Institution]]'s [[National Museum of Natural History]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Unknown|year=2003|title=From Across the Ocean|journal=Hornbill|pages=5–?}}</ref> He is also a Founding Fellow of the Indian Fisheries Association.{{Citation needed|date=September 2010}}<!-- web link does not give info of his being a Founding Fellow -->

From 1991 he guided MSc and PhD students and was a visiting faculty at the University of Mumbai. He served on the Board of Governors of [[Maharashtra]] Nature Parks Association for three years{{When|date=September 2010}} and was on the executive committee of the [[Bombay Natural History Society]] from 1988 to 2004.<ref name=":0" /> In 1994, he was awarded the Dharmakumarsinhji Trophy for his lifetime achievement in the field of [[ornamental fish]] keeping.

A [[Variety (biology)|variety]] of ''[[Sida acuta]]'' Burm., a plant discovered at [[Lakshadweep]] by Dr. M.R. Almeida was named after him as ''S. acuta var chhapgarii''.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Almeida, M.R. |year=1991|title=Additions to the terrestrial flora of Lakshadweep|journal=J. Bombay Nat. Hist. Soc. |volume=90|issue=1|pages=130–132}}</ref>

Sida albeida chhapgari:Javed Mohammed has named a new species of crab spider thomisus chhapgari after him.

==Publications==
Dr Chhapgar published numerous papers in scientific journals. He is a contributing editor to ''The Aquarium'' and [[Aquarium Fish International|Freshwater and Marine Aquarium]]. He also wrote several books and articles for a popular audience, some under the pen name of ''beefsea''.<ref name=":0" /> Some of his publications include:

* ''Marine Crabs of Bombay State''. Published by the Taraporevala Marine Biological Station, Bombay (1957)
* ''How to keep fish at home'' (in English, Hindi and Marathi). Taraporevala Aquarium Bombay. (sold over 10,000 copies in English)(1982).
* ''Guide to keeping and breeding aquarium fish''. Bombay Aquarium Society (1983).
* ''Common fishes of India''. Oxford University Press, India. (1987). {{ISBN|0-19-568799-X}}
* [http://www.arvindguptatoys.com/arvindgupta/25nbt-%20Wonder%20World%20Under%20Water%20by%20B.F.Chhapgar.pdf ''Wonder world under water'']. [[National Book Trust]], India.  (1991). {{ISBN|978-81-237-1477-6}}
* [http://www.oup.co.in/search_detail.php?id=144632 ''Seashore life of India'']. Oxford University Press, India (1991). {{ISBN|978-0-19-568800-9}}
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20100911154429/http://www.flipkart.com/man-inside-sea-chhapgar-book-8123715366 ''Man Inside the sea'']. National Book Trust, India (1995). {{ISBN|81-237-1536-6}}
* ''Guide to Taraporevala Aquarium''. Taraporevala Aquarium, Mumbai (1995).
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=y9kZAAAACAAJ ''Salim Ali’s India''], Bombay Natural History Society. (Edited jointly with Dr Ashok S. Kothari) (1996). {{ISBN|0-19-564160-4}}
*''[https://books.google.com/books?id=e_faAAAAMAAJ Treasures of Indian Wildlife]''{{dead link|date=July 2017|fix-attempted=yes}}. Bombay Natural History Society.  (Jointly edited with [https://www.sanctuaryasia.com/conservation/reviews/book-reviews/1216-treasures-of-indian-wildlife.html Dr. Ashok S Kothari]) (2005). {{ISBN|978-0-19-564227-8}}
* [http://www.oup.co.in/search_detail.php?id=143074 ''Marine life in India'']. Oxford University Press, India.  (2005–06). {{ISBN|978-0-19-568514-5}}
* [http://bnhs.org/article.php?cid=MjI%3D&sid=NTEw&aid=NTI5&t=Mg%3D%3D ''Living Jewels from the Indian Jungle'']{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. Bombay Natural History Society.  ([https://www.sanctuaryasia.com/conservation/reviews/book-reviews/2956-living-jewels-from-the-indian-jungle.html Edited jointly with Dr Ashok S Kothari]) (2009). {{ISBN|978-0-19-806465-7}}
* ''Understanding the sea''. Bombay Natural History Society. (2013).
* ''Wildlife of the Himalayas and the Terai Region'', Bombay Natural History Society. (Edited jointly with Dr. Ashok S Kothari) (2012).
* In press –   ''Wonders of a coral reef''. National Book Trust, India.

In the aftermath of heavy rains in Mumbai in August 2005, nearly 2,000 unsold copies of his book "The Marine Life in India" at the Oxford University Press warehouse were destroyed by flooding.<ref>The Times of India Mumbai; Date:4 August 2005; Section:Pg 04 – City; Page Number 4</ref>
